vibe.rationale: Vibe 3 — downgraded from 5. The May 26 upgrade to 5 rested on the reported Khamenei template endorsement (US intelligence characterization). Three compounding triggers drive the May 27 downgrade. First and primary: Shamkhani — Khamenei's direct advisor — called Trump's desired nuclear program control a 'fantasy' and characterized the situation as 'an olive branch we see only as barbed wire.' This is not a Tasnim/Fars editorial voice or a hardliner parliamentary faction; this is Khamenei's inner circle contradicting the specific nuclear-control dimension of the deal framework. Shamkhani's statement implies the May 26 Khamenei 'template endorsement' either (a) covered only non-nuclear deal elements — ceasefire, blockade lift, sanctions — or (b) the Supreme Leader's position has shifted since the US intelligence assessment, or (c) the intelligence characterization was imprecise. All three interpretations collapse the vibe-5 upgrade pillar. Second: Araghchi stated he was 'unsure whether a deal was imminent' — the Iranian FM walking back the deal-proximity framing. Third: April CPI came in at 3.8% YoY, above the 3.7% forecast, up from 3.3% in March, with energy +17.9% YoY — the worst energy inflation reading since September 2022. Core CPI hit 2.8% vs 2.7% forecast. The oil shock is embedding faster than prior readings. On Warsh Day 13, the Fed issued no communication on the hottest CPI print of 2026. The case against going lower than 3: Trump is explicitly optimistic ('close to finalizing with strong inspections'). Shamkhani said Iran is 'ready to sign in exchange for sanctions removal' — deal desire confirmed. The Gorge fire was contained. Deal is not dead. The case for 3 over 4: the Khamenei endorsement upgrade trigger is now directly contested by Khamenei's own advisor; the CPI miss worsens the Warsh communication vacuum; WPA T-2 with zero action. Vibe 3 is the landing. Return to 4 requires: Khamenei direct public statement or Iranian FM formal text confirming nuclear commitments survive Shamkhani challenge; or WPA emergency session announced. Drop to 2 requires: Shamkhani statement confirmed as Khamenei-authorized deal rejection; deal framework collapse; Warsh surprise hike signal; or CENTCOM repositioning indicating May 29 escalation.

items.headline: Shamkhani Calls Nuclear Control 'Fantasy'; Araghchi 'Unsure If Imminent'; Trump 'Close to Finalizing' — Khamenei Endorsement Signal Materially Undercut; WPA T-2 to May 29
items.summary: The Iran deal picture as of May 27 evening represents a qualified step back from yesterday's vibe-5 position. Three principal signals dominate. First: Ali Shamkhani, advisor to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, today dismissed Trump's desired control over Iran's nuclear program as a 'fantasy,' saying 'he speaks of an olive branch, but we see only barbed wire.' Shamkhani simultaneously confirmed Iran is 'ready to sign a nuclear deal in exchange for the quick removal of all financial sanctions' — signaling deal desire, but on terms that exclude US nuclear-program control. The analytical significance: Shamkhani is Khamenei's direct advisor, not a hardliner parliamentary faction or state-media editorial voice. His public rejection of the nuclear-control dimension directly complicates the May 26 US intelligence characterization that Khamenei 'endorsed the broad template.' The nuclear commitment language reported by Axios/CNN (May 25) — Iran agrees to never pursue nuclear weapons, negotiate enrichment suspension, negotiate HEU removal — is the specific architecture that Shamkhani's 'fantasy' characterization contests. Second: Iranian FM Araghchi stated he was 'unsure whether a deal was imminent' — the FM contradicting the deal-proximity framing from both Trump and yesterday's US intelligence signal. Third: Trump said both sides are 'close to finalizing an agreement involving strong inspections' — the most specific inspection-framework language he has publicly used. The deal is not dead; the parties remain engaged. But the core unresolved tension — US nuclear-program control vs. Iran's sovereignty framing — has been restated publicly by Khamenei's inner circle in the most pointed language of the negotiation cycle. WPA: The 90-day hard deadline is now 48 hours away. Congress is in session (Day 2 post-Memorial Day). No emergency session, no pre-deadline House vote, no Senate 10th resolution has been announced. The Senate has now rejected nine WPA resolutions since March. Multiple Democrats have raised the possibility of suing Trump if hostilities continue past May 29. The administration's 'hostilities terminated' posture does not survive Day 90 plain-text scrutiny; the naval blockade, CENTCOM self-defense strikes, and physical Hormuz closure are operative regardless of deal status.

items.headline: I-84 Biggs Junction Fire Contained — First PNW Corridor-Level Fire Infrastructure Event of 2026 Season; SE WA 250 Acres; CISA Day 24 Clean; Oregon Fire Day 20; T-5 to June 1
items.summary: The infrastructure picture on May 27 is anchored by the Biggs Junction corridor fire event. A wildfire erupted on May 24 (Saturday) near Biggs Junction along the I-84 corridor in Sherman County, Oregon — briefly closing all lanes of Interstate 84 near milepost 105 east of Biggs Junction. Fast-moving flames, heavy smoke, and dangerous visibility caused multiple vehicle crashes during the closure. Crews contained the fire by Saturday evening and I-84 reopened. Simultaneously, a separate fire burned 250 acres in southeastern Washington state on May 24. The Biggs Junction fire is analytically significant as the first corridor-level transportation infrastructure event of the 2026 fire season — I-84 through the Columbia Gorge is the primary freight and passenger artery connecting Portland to inland Oregon, Washington, and Idaho. The event confirms fire activity emerging from the Columbia Gorge before the NIFC June 1 above-normal onset threshold for eastern Oregon and Washington. Post-Memorial Day assessment (May 26-27 morning reports from ODF, BLM, NWS) is the operative monitoring window for any holiday ignitions. Oregon fire season advances to Day 20: Level 1 Central Oregon restrictions (Deschutes, Ochoco, Crooked River) at Day 10 (effective May 18); BLM full OR/WA restrictions at Day 14 (effective May 14); campfire bans operative across both systems. June 1 east Cascades above-normal onset is T-5 days. CISA maintains its clean streak at Day 24. No FBI IC3 flash, no OT/ICS incident. The Shamkhani nuclear-rejection statement today modestly re-elevates IRGC-aligned cyber risk — if IRGC institutional actors interpret the 'fantasy' statement as a Khamenei inner-circle rejection of the deal nuclear dimension, the IRGC hardliner rejection-signal cyber vector from May 25 is partially reinstated. Standard elevated monitoring is the appropriate posture.
